newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Brollies for guests if it rains at HK handover.
newsitem.headline: Brollies for guests if it rains at HK handover.

text.p: Umbrellas will be given to each of the 10,000 guests attending outdoor ceremonies marking the handover of Hong Kong to China on the evening of June 30 if it rains, a newspaper said on Sunday.
Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten is scheduled to deliver his valedictory address at the event, an extravaganza of pomp and circumstance, on the waterfront of Hong Kong island.

"If there is heavy rain, then we can do nothing but cancel it. However, if there are just showers, then we have prepared 10,000 umbrellas for our guests," Stephen Lam, coordinator for the handover ceremony, told the South China Morning Post.
Patten will also attend the solemn flag ceremony at midnight when the British relinquish sovereignty of Hong Kong to China.
Prince Charles will preside over the occasion, which marks the end of a 156-year colonial era.
President Jiang Zemin will represent China.
Hong Kong's Royal Observatory -- which will drop its Royal prefix on July 1 -- has said there is a good chance it will rain on the day.
